To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DmSetdb is responsible for mono- or trimethylation of histone H4K9 during Drosophyla spermatogenesis.

dG9a is localized in the cytoplams during spermatogenesis and in nuclei of early canoe stage spermatids, and that the dG9a-mediated H3K9 methylation is not essential for spermatogenesis, although DmSETDB and SU(VAR)-3–9 are responsible for H3K9 monomethylation and trimethylation, respectively.
dG9a plays a minor role in spermatogenesis, while DmSETDB plays an important role in spermatocyte development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of H3K4 methylation in Drosophilas spermatogenesis.
the roles of H3K methyltransferases during spermatogenesis in a model organism.
the roles of H3K4-specific HMTases during Drosphila spermatogenesis, which is an important issue for understanding the epigenetic regulation of germ line development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DmSETDB2, not dG9a and SU(VAR)-3–9, is the most critical H3K9 HMTase for spermatogenesis.
dG9a and SU(VAR)-mediated H3K4 trimethylation are dispensable for male fertility.
H3K9 methylation is not essential for spermatogenesis but is important for gene expression in DrosophILA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dG9a is dispensable, but DmSETDB and SU(VAR3)3-9 are essential for spermatogenesis.
dG9a may be involved in epigenetic regulation of spermatogenesis, but not in X–Y chromosome segregation.

H3K9 methylation is not a critical factor for spermatogenesis and that the H3K9 HMTases may have other roles in Drosophla spermatogenesis, including the regulation of spermatogenesis-specific gene expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the H3K9 methylation status in the nuclei of Drosophila sperm is not essential for spermatogenesis.
Drosophila H3K9 HMTases are involved in epigenetic control of gene expression in male germ line cells, but not in X–Y chromosome segregation.
the roles of H3K27 methyltransferases in spermatogenesis may be conserved between mammals and Drosophila, but the functions of H3K36 and H3K9 HMTases are likely to be distinct between these species.
